Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` parameters of `APIRouter`

This fixes the issue reported in this comment: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14851#issuecomment-3863896385

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI


def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)


app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])


@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"ok": True}
```

According to the issue description and Starlette's routing implementation, this can lead to these parameters being overridden or not properly handled if the base class also initializes them. Specifically, `APIRouter.__init__` should call `super().__init__` first and then set its own state to ensure the initialization sequence is correct.

FILES: fastapi/routing.py:961-983

ROOT CAUSE: `APIRouter.__init__` sets `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` before calling `super().__init__`, which can cause them to be overridden by the base class `Router` initialization in some versions of Starlette or under certain conditions.

CHANGE: Move the calls to `super().__init__` before the assignments of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown`.
